questions.question_text: Which memory management scheme allows the physical address space of a process to be non-contiguous?
What occurs when a CPU attempts to access a page that is mapped into the virtual address space but not loaded into physical RAM?
In HTTP communications, which response status code range represents Client Errors?
Which mechanism is used by modern web applications to safely transmit claims between two parties as a JSON object?
Which CPU scheduling algorithm gives the lowest average waiting time for a given set of processes?
What is a deadlock in operating systems?
options: A state where two or more processes are each waiting for a resource held by another, forming a cycle with no progress
A process that has finished executing but not been removed from memory
A scheduling algorithm that never terminates
An error caused by insufficient CPU cache

questions.question_text: Which of the four Coffman conditions is NOT required for a deadlock to occur?
What is the main difference between a process and a thread?
options: Threads within the same process share the same memory space, while processes have separate memory spaces
Threads cannot run concurrently, but processes can
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable

questions.question_text: Which synchronization primitive uses an integer counter to control access to a shared resource by multiple processes?
What is 'thrashing' in the context of virtual memory?
options: Excessive paging activity that causes the system to spend most of its time swapping pages instead of executing processes
A CPU running at maximum clock speed continuously
A hard disk failure due to overheating
Two threads writing to the same variable simultaneously

questions.question_text: Which HTTP method is idempotent and safe, typically used to retrieve a resource without modifying server state?
What does REST stand for in the context of web API architecture?
Which HTTP status code indicates that a resource was successfully created?
What is the purpose of CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) in web browsers?
options: To control which external origins are permitted to make requests to a server's resources
To encrypt data sent over HTTPS
To compress HTTP responses for faster delivery
To cache static assets on the client

questions.question_text: Which protocol translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses?
In a client-server web architecture, what is the primary role of a load balancer?
options: To distribute incoming network traffic across multiple servers to prevent overload

questions.question_text: What distinguishes HTTPS from HTTP?
options: HTTPS encrypts data in transit using TLS/SSL, while HTTP does not
HTTPS is faster because it skips the TCP handshake
HTTPS only works with static websites
HTTPS does not support POST requests

questions.question_text: Which OS scheduling technique allocates a fixed time slice to each process in a cyclic order?
What is the main purpose of a cookie in web architecture?
options: To store small pieces of state (like session data) on the client, sent back to the server with each request
To permanently store large files on the client

questions.question_text: Which OS concept refers to giving a process the illusion of a very large, contiguous memory space, backed partly by disk?
What is the purpose of an API Gateway in a microservices web architecture?
options: To act as a single entry point that routes client requests to the appropriate backend microservices
To store the entire application's database
To compile microservices into a single monolith
